note: What each detected box on the two query photographs is. These photographs contribute nothing to the catalog: their references come from the video and from the four earlier photographs, so a correct name here is recognition and not recall.  Badges 9 and 10 of IMG_0252 were unlabelled while the frame carried ten boxes, so badge alignment silently skipped two badges on the second-hardest photograph here. Both are the Fuji bag: badge 10's crop reads WEST GROWN / FUJI / Sure to core! over Net Wt 48 oz (3 lb) Extra Fancy, and badge 9 is the same red apples through the clear half of that bag. They are labelled purple_produce_bag because that is the SKU the index is built on, which the SAME map in census-live.ts already reads as the Fuji bag.
out_of_catalog: a real product the catalog does not contain. The right answer for these is to decline, and they are what makes the floor measurable at all.
not_a_product: the shopper's own tote bag, and boxes drawn across several items at once

corrections: IMG_0254 badge 10 was labelled purple_produce_bag and holds the asparagus bag. The crop is green stalks in plastic filling the box, with a sliver of purple wrapper at the left edge, which is what the original reading caught. Two independent readings agree it is asparagus: this crop, and the hand-labelled box in corpus/kart/boxes-IMG_0254.json, placed before the badge label was examined. The correction is score-neutral on every pass observed, because the census named this badge 'vegetables', 'bagged produce' or 'vegetable tray', and none of those matches either label's word set. It is made for attribution, not for the number: with the wrong label the asparagus miss reads as a detection failure, and it is a naming failure on a correctly isolated badge.
